newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Transnet's rail subsidiary Spoornet is to announce a broad restructuring on Friday focusing on a management reshuffle and opening its operations to the private sector, analysts said.
- September car sales fell 9.5 percent to 19,928 units against the corresponding month last year after lower economic activity and punitive interest rates affected the vehicle market.

- The money market shortage jumped more than one billion rand to just under 10 billion rand this week -- its highest level for five months and close to the figure that resulted in commercial banks' controversial rates hike in May.
- Former law and order mnister Adriaan Vlok will on Friday become the first apartheid-era cabinet minister to be subpoenaed by the Truth Commission.

- Disgruntled minorities in Rainbow Chicken have shown a remarkable lack of faith in the company by putting up less than one percent of the capital for a 750 million rand rights offer to recapitalise the ailing broiler producer.
- Irregular and obstructive trading practises by South Africa's food giants have cost South Africa billions of rand in exports, the Independent Exporters' Association said.
- South African fund managers said the asset swaps that they had entered into did not contravene U.S. legislation.
- The Reserve Bank denied reports that the Community Bank was set for liquidation.
- The Truth and Reconciliation Commission will begin issuing subpoenas to former law and order minister Adriaan Vlok and high-ranking policemen, including four former commissioners.
- Kruger National Park officials are confident of a rapid recovery of valuable grazing land after fires destroyed about 200,000 hectares this week.
